title: Sole Proprietorship Ownership and Management
context: Analyze how a sole proprietorship concentrates ownership and operational control in a single individual. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship is a business owned by one person who also manages and runs the business.
The sole proprietor can make all management decisions without necessarily having to consider other opinions.
Because the business is not a legal entity of its own, profits are reported on the owner's personal income tax statement.
A sole proprietorship is a separate legal person that files corporate income tax independently of the owner.
Retirement or long-term illness of the sole proprietor may create continuity problems for the business.
tactical_explanations:
A sole proprietorship puts ownership and day-to-day running in one natural person. That person is both owner and manager — no co-owners and no separate board.

So the statement is True.

Decision rights sit undivided with the proprietor. Advice can be taken, but other opinions are not a formal requirement before acting.

So the statement is True.

The firm is not a separate legal person, so trading profit is not taxed on a corporate return. It lands on the owner’s personal income tax statement.

So the statement is True.

A sole proprietorship is not a separate legal person. Corporate personality and an independent corporate tax filing belong to incorporated companies, not to a sole trader.

Counterexample: the bakery owner reports bakery profit on a personal return, not as a corporation.

So the statement is False.

Continuity hangs on one person’s capacity to own and manage. Retirement or long-term illness can interrupt operations unless ownership and control are transferred.

So the statement is True.

title: Establishment Requirements and Liability Exposure
context: Consider a neighbourhood bakery operated as a sole proprietorship with one owner-manager and a small team of assistants. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sole proprietorships are easy to establish, especially for small businesses, because there are no financial requirements to start this kind of business.
Limited liability protects the sole proprietor's private assets so creditors may claim only assets formally recorded as business property.
Unlimited liability means creditors may reach the proprietor's personal property when business debts must be repaid.
Incorporating as a sole proprietorship grants the owner limited liability equal to the capital originally invested.
Trade credit from suppliers eliminates the sole proprietor's liability for those purchase obligations.
tactical_explanations:
For small ventures, start-up as a sole trader needs no minimum capital deposit. That low formal hurdle is why the form is described as easy to establish.

So the statement is True.

Sole traders face unlimited liability. Creditors are not confined to assets labelled “business property”; private wealth can be reached when debts remain unpaid.

So the statement is False.

Unlimited liability means repayment duty follows the owner personally. If firm cash is short, personal property can be used to settle business debts.

So the statement is True.

Calling the firm a sole proprietorship does not create limited liability or treat capital invested as a liability cap. Limited liability is a corporate feature, not a sole-trader one.

So the statement is False.

Trade credit only defers payment; it does not cancel the obligation. Supplier balances remain debts the proprietor must honour.

So the statement is False.

title: Legal Status and Tax Treatment
context: Review the legal and fiscal position of a sole proprietorship compared with incorporated business forms. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship is not a legal entity of its own separate from the business owner.
The owner pays tax on the profits that are earned from the business through the personal income tax statement.
Management of the business largely depends on the sole proprietor, who retains responsibility for the most important decisions.
Because profits pass directly to the owner for tax purposes, the business cannot hire employees or enter supplier contracts.
If the sole proprietor needs support, he or she can hire personnel while still bearing the central management role.
tactical_explanations:
Unlike a corporation, a sole proprietorship has no legal personality apart from the owner. Contracts and assets attach to that person.

So the statement is True.

Profits are taxed as the owner’s personal income. The personal tax statement — not a separate corporate return — carries the business profit.

So the statement is True.

Day-to-day and strategic control concentrate on the proprietor. The most important decisions stay with that one owner-manager.

So the statement is True.

Pass-through tax treatment does not block hiring or supplier contracts. A sole trader can employ staff and buy on account while still reporting profit personally.

So the statement is False.

Extra hands are allowed. Hired personnel support operations, yet the proprietor keeps the central management role and the associated risk.

So the statement is True.

title: Single Owner Control and Staffing
context: Analyze management authority within a sole proprietorship when the owner employs assistants for daily operations. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The sole proprietor may hire personnel when additional support is required to run the business.
Hiring staff transfers unlimited liability for business debts entirely to the employees rather than the owner.
Even with hired personnel, it remains the sole proprietor's task to make the most important management decisions and take all the risk.
The sole proprietor can make all management decisions and does not necessarily have to consider other opinions.
Continuity of the business may be disrupted when the sole proprietor cannot continue managing due to long-term illness.
tactical_explanations:
When workload exceeds what one person can cover, the proprietor may hire staff. Employment does not change the sole-trader legal form.

So the statement is True.

Staff wages do not shift debt risk. Unlimited liability for business obligations stays with the owner, not with employees.

So the statement is False.

Assistants can run tills or handle deliveries, but the proprietor still makes the key management calls and bears the full risk.

So the statement is True.

Undivided ownership means undivided decision rights. The owner need not clear choices with co-owners — there are none.

So the statement is True.

Long-term illness of the only owner-manager can halt continuity. The business depends on that person’s capacity to keep managing.

So the statement is True.

title: Misconceptions About Sole Trader Status
context: Review common claims about what sole proprietorship status implies for liability, taxation, and legal personality. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Registering a business name as a sole proprietorship converts the firm into an incorporated legal person with its own tax identity.
Profits earned by a sole proprietorship are directly reported on the business owner's personal income tax statement.
A sole proprietorship requires substantial minimum share capital before the owner may begin trading legally.
Limited liability protects a sole proprietor's private home from creditors when business debts exceed available firm assets.
Two persons who wish to share tasks and risk equally should choose a sole proprietorship rather than a partnership.
tactical_explanations:
A trading name on a sole proprietorship is still just a label for the owner’s business. It does not create an incorporated legal person with its own tax identity.

So the statement is False.

Profit flows straight onto the owner’s personal income tax statement because the firm lacks separate legal personality.

So the statement is True.

Sole traders face no substantial minimum share capital before trading. That capital hurdle belongs to companies, not to this unincorporated form.

So the statement is False.

Limited liability does not protect a sole trader’s private home. If business debts exceed firm assets, personal property remains exposed.

So the statement is False.

Equal sharing of tasks and risk needs two (or more) owners — a partnership. A sole proprietorship has only one owner by definition.

So the statement is False.

title: Continuity Risk and Decision Authority
context: Consider operational continuity when a sole trader plans retirement after years of running a local repair workshop. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship automatically continues unchanged when the owner retires without any transfer arrangement.
Continuity problems may occur if the sole proprietor wants to retire or suffers a long-term illness.
Because one person owns and manages the firm, succession planning is always simpler than in structures with transferable shares.
Retirement of the sole proprietor has no effect on business continuity because staff can legally assume ownership without transfer.
The management of the business largely depends on the sole proprietor, who retains the most important decision rights.
tactical_explanations:
Retirement does not leave the firm running on autopilot. Without a transfer of ownership and management, the sole proprietorship does not simply continue unchanged.

So the statement is False.

Because control sits with one person, retirement or long-term illness can create real continuity problems for the workshop.

So the statement is True.

“Always simpler” overstates succession. Shares in a company can transfer more cleanly; a sole trader’s retirement still needs an explicit hand-over of the business.

So the statement is False.

Staff cannot legally assume ownership just by continuing to work. Ownership must be transferred; retirement without that step breaks continuity.

So the statement is False.

Management still depends on the proprietor. The most important decision rights remain with that single owner-manager.

So the statement is True.

title: Unlimited Liability in Practice
context: Analyze how creditor claims against a failing sole proprietorship may extend beyond business assets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The sole proprietor is liable for all debts and obligations of the business under unlimited liability.
Unlimited liability applies only to short-term trade credit and not to long-term bank loans secured by property.
Creditors usually ask for assets that can serve as collateral, especially for long-term credit.
Private assets of the sole proprietor are also at stake if the business fails and debts need to be repaid.
Pledging collateral for a bank loan fully exempts all remaining private assets from any further creditor claims.
tactical_explanations:
Unlimited liability covers every business debt and obligation. The proprietor stands behind them all.

So the statement is True.

Unlimited liability is not limited to trade credit. Long-term bank loans — even those secured on property — remain personal obligations of the sole trader.

So the statement is False.

Lenders often want pledgeable assets, especially on long-term facilities. Collateral is a standard condition for that kind of credit.

So the statement is True.

If the firm fails and debts remain, private assets are also at stake. That is the practical meaning of unlimited liability.

So the statement is True.

Pledging collateral does not fence off every other private asset. Creditors can still pursue remaining personal wealth if the secured asset does not cover the debt.

So the statement is False.

title: Personal Taxation of Business Profits
context: Review how fiscal treatment links sole proprietorship earnings to the owner's personal tax affairs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Because the sole proprietorship is not a legal entity, profits are reported on the owner's personal income tax statement.
Operating as a sole proprietorship exempts the owner from income tax on business profits entirely.
The owner pays tax on the profits earned from the business rather than through a separate corporate tax return.
Business profits and the proprietor's other personal income may appear on the same personal tax assessment.
Separate legal personality is required before profits can be taxed as personal income of the owner.
tactical_explanations:
No separate legal entity means no separate corporate tax shell. Business profit is reported on the owner’s personal income tax statement.

So the statement is True.

Sole-trader status does not wipe out tax on profits. The owner still pays income tax on what the business earns.

So the statement is False.

Tax is assessed on the individual, not through a corporate return. The proprietor pays on business profits as personal income.

So the statement is True.

Business profit and other personal income can sit on the same personal assessment. That is how pass-through taxation works for sole traders.

So the statement is True.

Separate legal personality is not a precondition for personal taxation of profits. Sole traders are taxed personally precisely because they lack that personality.

So the statement is False.

title: Core Features of Sole Trader Businesses
context: Analyze the defining characteristics of sole proprietorship as described in business ownership theory. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship combines ownership and day-to-day management in a single individual without separate partners.
Sole proprietorships are easy to establish, especially for small businesses, with no financial requirements to start.
The business is not a legal entity of its own, so profits are taxed on the owner's personal income statement.
Unlimited liability means the sole proprietor's private assets are also at stake when business debts must be repaid.
If the sole proprietor needs support, personnel may be hired while the proprietor retains key management decisions.
tactical_explanations:
One individual owns the firm and runs it day to day. There are no partners splitting ownership or management.

So the statement is True.

Start-up is light on formal finance hurdles: no minimum capital is required, which suits many small businesses.

So the statement is True.

Without its own legal personality, the firm’s profit is taxed on the owner’s personal income statement.

So the statement is True.

Unlimited liability puts private assets on the line when business debts must be repaid beyond firm resources.

So the statement is True.

Personnel can be hired for support, yet key management decisions stay with the proprietor.

So the statement is True.

title: Legal Personality and Liability Distinctions
context: Review distinctions between unincorporated sole traders and incorporated companies regarding legal status and creditor protection. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship lacks the separate legal personality that allows a corporation to sue and be sued in its own name.
Profits of a sole proprietorship are reported on the business owner's personal income tax statement.
Under unlimited liability, creditors may pursue the proprietor's private assets when business debts remain unpaid.
Easy establishment with no capital requirements makes sole proprietorships accessible for small businesses.
Continuity problems may arise if the sole proprietor suffers a long-term illness or wishes to retire.
tactical_explanations:
A corporation can sue and be sued in its own name. A sole proprietorship cannot — it has no separate legal personality.

So the statement is True.

Profit reporting follows the owner’s personal income tax statement, not a company return.

So the statement is True.

When business debts remain unpaid, unlimited liability lets creditors pursue private assets of the proprietor.

So the statement is True.

No capital threshold blocks entry. That ease of establishment is why sole trading suits many small start-ups.

So the statement is True.

Long-term illness or retirement of the only owner-manager can interrupt continuity of the business.

So the statement is True.

title: Management Concentration and Risk Bearing
context: Consider a freelance designer operating as a sole proprietorship who occasionally contracts administrative help. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The sole proprietor can make all management decisions without necessarily consulting other owners.
It remains the sole proprietor's task to make the most important management decisions and take all the risk.
Management of the business largely depends on the sole proprietor rather than on a separate board of directors.
Even when administrative tasks are delegated, the proprietor retains authority over the most important management decisions.
Hiring personnel means the employees rather than the proprietor decide the firm's strategic direction.
tactical_explanations:
With no co-owners, the designer need not clear decisions with other equity holders. All management decisions can be taken alone.

So the statement is True.

Even with occasional administrative help, the most important decisions and all of the risk stay with the proprietor.

So the statement is True.

There is no board of directors in this form. Management depends on the sole proprietor personally.

So the statement is True.

Delegating paperwork does not surrender strategic control. Authority over the most important management decisions remains with the owner.

So the statement is True.

Hired help does not take over strategic direction. Employees support operations; the proprietor still sets the firm’s course.

So the statement is False.

title: Establishment Ease and Business Continuity
context: Analyze why sole proprietorships appeal for small start-ups yet pose succession challenges over time. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sole proprietorships are easy to establish because there are no financial requirements to start this kind of business.
A sole proprietorship is owned and managed by one person who bears the central operational responsibility.
Stepping away through retirement or prolonged illness may interrupt continuity in a sole proprietorship.
Extra money can be sought from investors and/or from banks when personal funds prove insufficient.
Because the firm is not a legal entity, profits are taxed on the owner's personal income tax statement.
tactical_explanations:
No financial requirements must be met before trading as a sole proprietor. That is the establishment advantage for small start-ups.

So the statement is True.

Ownership and central operational responsibility sit with one person who both owns and manages the firm.

So the statement is True.

Stepping away through retirement or prolonged illness can interrupt continuity when everything hangs on that one manager.

So the statement is True.

When personal funds run short, extra money can be sought from investors and/or banks — external finance options for the sole trader.

So the statement is True.

Lacking separate legal personality, profits are taxed on the owner’s personal income tax statement.

So the statement is True.

title: Creditor Claims and Collateral Exposure
context: Review how secured and unsecured borrowing affects a sole proprietor when revenue falls short of repayment obligations. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Listing a trading name transforms a sole proprietorship into a corporation with its own legal personality.
A sole proprietorship remains unincorporated even when the owner registers for tax and hires multiple employees.
The sole proprietor pays personal income tax on business profits because the business is not a legal entity of its own.
All kinds of credit, short-term as well as long-term, are liabilities for the sole proprietor.
Collateral requirements apply only to internal sources of finance such as retained profit.
tactical_explanations:
A trading name is only a business style. It does not transform a sole proprietorship into a corporation with its own legal personality.

So the statement is False.

Tax registration and a payroll do not incorporate the firm. The sole proprietorship stays unincorporated despite employees and tax filings.

So the statement is True.

Because the business is not a legal entity of its own, the proprietor pays personal income tax on business profits.

So the statement is True.

Short-term and long-term credit alike are liabilities of the sole proprietor. Duration does not remove the obligation.

So the statement is True.

Collateral is a lender’s condition on external borrowing, not on internal finance. Retained profit does not require pledged assets.

So the statement is False.

title: Ownership Structure Compared With Partnership
context: Analyze when sole proprietorship is appropriate versus partnership for persons planning a jointly managed venture. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship suits one owner who both manages the business and accepts the associated risk.
A sole proprietorship allows two equal co-owners to divide management rights without a partnership agreement.
A sole proprietorship is the appropriate structure when several investors seek limited liability through transferable shares.
Two persons who want to share tasks and risk with equal rights would better realise their business as a partnership.
Partnerships are unnecessary when two founders can rely on sole proprietorship rules to share ownership equally.
tactical_explanations:
One owner who manages and accepts the risk fits sole proprietorship by design.

So the statement is True.

Two equal co-owners need a partnership structure and agreement. Sole proprietorship has a single owner — it cannot split management rights between two equals.

So the statement is False.

Limited liability through transferable shares is a corporate story. Sole proprietorship offers neither limited liability nor share transfer for several investors.

So the statement is False.

Sharing tasks and risk with equal rights points to partnership. That is the structure Tina-and-Steve-style founders should use.

So the statement is True.

Sole proprietorship rules do not create equal co-ownership for two founders. Partnership is the form that shares ownership properly.

So the statement is False.

title: Tax Reporting Without Corporate Personality
context: Review fiscal consequences when a business lacks separate legal personality from its owner. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Business profits of an unincorporated sole trader flow directly onto the owner's personal income tax statement.
The owner pays tax on profits earned from the business because the firm is not a separate legal entity.
Personal income tax treatment means the sole proprietorship must issue dividends to the owner before tax is due.
Operating without corporate personality does not exempt the proprietor from tax on business profits.
A separate corporate tax return is required for every sole proprietorship regardless of legal status.
tactical_explanations:
Unincorporated status sends business profits straight onto the owner’s personal income tax statement.

So the statement is True.

The firm is not a separate legal entity, so the owner pays tax on profits earned from the business as personal income.

So the statement is True.

Sole traders do not pay themselves dividends before tax is due. Profit is taxed as personal income without a corporate dividend step.

So the statement is False.

Missing corporate personality does not create a tax holiday. The proprietor still owes tax on business profits.

So the statement is True.

A separate corporate tax return is not required for a sole proprietorship. Personal taxation replaces that corporate filing.

So the statement is False.

title: Liability Scope Across Credit Types
context: Consider a sole trader using supplier trade credit, a bank overdraft, and a property-backed long-term loan simultaneously. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Trade credit from a supplier never requires repayment because deferred payment is a grant from the supplier.
Trade credit from a supplier creates a short-term liability that the sole proprietor must honour.
Long-term bank loans secured by land are excluded from unlimited liability because collateral protects the owner completely.
If the business fails, private assets are also at stake when debts need to be repaid beyond available business funds.
All kinds of credit, whether short-term or long-term, remain obligations of the sole proprietor.
tactical_explanations:
Deferred payment is still a debt. Trade credit is not a grant; the supplier expects repayment of the purchase price.

So the statement is False.

Supplier trade credit is a short-term liability. The sole proprietor must honour the outstanding balance when due.

So the statement is True.

Collateral on a land-backed loan does not carve that debt out of unlimited liability. The loan remains an obligation; private exposure can remain if collateral falls short.

So the statement is False.

Failure that leaves debts unpaid puts private assets at stake once business funds are exhausted.

So the statement is True.

Whether the facility lasts months or years, credit remains an obligation of the sole proprietor.

So the statement is True.

title: Single-Owner Misclassification Traps
context: Review assertions that confuse sole proprietorship with incorporated or partnership structures. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Registering a commercial trading name automatically gives a sole proprietorship separate corporate legal personality.
Two friends planning equal management shares should form a sole proprietorship rather than a partnership.
Because the firm lacks separate legal personality, business profits are assessed as the proprietor's personal income.
Incorporated limited liability automatically applies once a sole trader opens a business bank account.
Hiring several employees automatically incorporates a sole proprietorship as a limited liability company.
tactical_explanations:
A commercial trading name does not automatically create separate corporate legal personality for a sole trader.

So the statement is False.

Equal management shares for two friends call for a partnership. A sole proprietorship admits only one owner.

So the statement is False.

Lacking separate legal personality, business profits are assessed as the proprietor’s personal income.

So the statement is True.

Opening a business bank account does not switch on incorporated limited liability. The legal form stays sole trader unless the business is actually incorporated.

So the statement is False.

A larger payroll does not incorporate the firm. Hiring employees leaves a sole proprietorship unincorporated and without automatic limited liability.

So the statement is False.

title: Basic Establishment and Tax Facts
context: Analyze foundational facts about starting and taxing a sole proprietorship. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Mandatory minimum share capital must be deposited before any sole proprietorship may legally commence trading.
A sole proprietorship is a separate legal person that must file corporate income tax independently of the owner.
Limited liability protects the sole proprietor when business debts exceed assets held in the business name.
The owner pays tax on profits earned from the business through personal income taxation.
Corporate income tax is assessed on sole proprietorship profits in a separate return from the owner's personal affairs.
tactical_explanations:
No mandatory minimum share capital must be deposited before a sole proprietorship may trade. That requirement belongs to companies.

So the statement is False.

A sole proprietorship is not a separate legal person and does not file corporate income tax independently of the owner.

So the statement is False.

Limited liability is not a sole-trader protection. When debts exceed business assets, private wealth remains exposed.

So the statement is False.

The owner pays tax on profits through personal income taxation — the standard fiscal treatment for this form.

So the statement is True.

Sole proprietorship profits are not assessed on a separate corporate return. They sit with the owner’s personal tax affairs.

So the statement is False.

title: Integrated Sole Trader Profile
context: Review the combined legal, managerial, and fiscal profile of a typical sole proprietorship. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: One person owns, manages, and runs the business while retaining the most important decision authority.
Without separate legal personality, business profits are assessed on the owner's personal income tax statement.
No minimum capital requirement applies when establishing a sole proprietorship for a small business.
Unlimited liability means private assets are also at stake if business debts must be repaid.
Continuity problems may occur when the sole proprietor retires or suffers long-term illness.
tactical_explanations:
One person owns, manages, and runs the business, keeping the most important decision authority.

So the statement is True.

Without separate legal personality, business profits are assessed on the owner’s personal income tax statement.

So the statement is True.

Small sole traders face no minimum capital requirement at establishment.

So the statement is True.

Unlimited liability means private assets are also at stake if business debts must be repaid.

So the statement is True.

Retirement or long-term illness of the sole proprietor can create continuity problems for the firm.

So the statement is True.

title: Finance Classification Nuances
context: Analyze how internal and external sources of finance apply to a sole proprietorship funding expansion. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained profit reinvested in the business counts as an internal source of finance for the sole proprietorship.
The owner's initial investment from personal savings is classified as an external source of finance.
Retained earnings and sale of unused assets are external sources because they originate outside the business.
Bank credit is internal finance for a sole proprietorship because borrowed money is deposited in the business bank account.
Internal sources of finance avoid financial charges such as interest that apply to borrowed funds.
tactical_explanations:
Profit kept in the business and ploughed back into operations is internal finance.

So the statement is True.

Personal savings put in at the start come from outside the firm’s own operations. In this chapter’s classification, the owner’s investment is an external source.

So the statement is True.

Retained earnings and sales of unused assets are generated inside the business. They are internal sources, not external ones.

So the statement is False.

Bank credit is money owed to an outside lender. Depositing the loan in the business account does not make borrowing internal finance.

So the statement is False.

Internal funds carry no interest bill to a creditor. That absence of financial charges is their advantage over borrowed money.

So the statement is True.

title: Short-Term and Long-Term Credit Instruments
context: Review credit instruments commonly available to sole proprietors from banks and suppliers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A bank overdraft is a flexible short-term credit instrument once a business bank account has been opened.
Trade credit allows a business to defer payment for purchases according to an agreement with the supplier.
Interest on a bank overdraft is paid only when the account is overdrawn.
Long-term bank loans are often based on land and property serving as collateral through a mortgage arrangement.
Trade credit from suppliers is classified as long-term debt finance because payment is deferred.
tactical_explanations:
After a current account exists, an overdraft can supply flexible short-term credit when cash is tight.

So the statement is True.

Under a supplier agreement, purchases need not be paid at once. Trade credit defers settlement for an agreed period.

So the statement is True.

Overdraft interest runs only while the account is overdrawn — not on a positive balance.

So the statement is True.

Long-term bank loans frequently use land and property as mortgage collateral.

So the statement is True.

Deferred supplier payment is still short-term trade credit, not long-term debt finance. Duration of the credit period keeps it in the short-term category.

So the statement is False.

title: Starting Capital and Owner Savings
context: Consider a new sole trader who funds start-up costs primarily from personal savings before seeking bank support. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Most sole proprietors invest their own savings in their business as an external source of finance.
If the sole proprietor lacks financial funds, setting up the business will be very difficult.
Personal savings invested at start-up are internal finance because they are generated from earlier business profits.
No financial requirements to start a sole proprietorship mean the owner never contributes personal capital.
Financial capability of the sole proprietor has no bearing on funds available to the business.
tactical_explanations:
Most sole proprietors begin with their own savings. That owner investment is classified as an external source of finance.

So the statement is True.

Funds available to the firm lean heavily on the proprietor’s own means. Thin personal finance makes start-up very difficult.

So the statement is True.

Personal savings at launch are not earlier business profits. They arrive from outside trading, so they are external — not internal — finance.

So the statement is False.

“No financial requirements” means no legal minimum capital, not that the owner never puts money in. Personal capital is still typically contributed.

So the statement is False.

The proprietor’s financial capability largely determines what funds the business can raise. Capability has a direct bearing on available finance.

So the statement is False.

title: Internal Versus External Finance Boundaries
context: Analyze classification of finance sources once a sole proprietorship is operating and generating revenue. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sale of assets that are no longer needed is classified as external finance provided by creditors.
The owner's investment from savings is internal finance because the owner and the business are the same legal person.
Retained profit that is reinvested rather than withdrawn by the proprietor supplies internal finance.
Investor funds and creditor loans from banks are internal sources because they are deposited in the business account.
Internal sources of finance require paying market interest rates to the proprietor acting as a lender.
tactical_explanations:
Selling unused assets releases cash from within the business. That is internal finance, not external money from creditors.

So the statement is False.

Owner savings are external in this classification even though owner and firm share one legal person. Internal finance starts from operating surplus and similar inside sources.

So the statement is False.

Profit kept in the firm and reinvested instead of withdrawn is the classic internal source once trading is under way.

So the statement is True.

Investors and bank creditors stand outside the firm. Their funds are external sources even when the cash sits in the business account.

So the statement is False.

Internal finance is valued precisely because it avoids market interest to a lender. The proprietor is not treated as an interest-charging creditor for retained funds.

So the statement is False.

title: Comprehensive Finance and Liability Picture
context: Review how sole proprietors combine internal funds, owner investment, and creditor finance while bearing personal liability. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The owner's investment and funds from investors and creditors are external sources of finance.
Retained profit and sale of unneeded assets are internal sources of finance once operations generate surplus.
All kinds of credit, short-term and long-term, are liabilities for the sole proprietor.
If revenues exceed expenses, profit can be retained and reinvested unless the sole proprietor withdraws it.
Unlimited liability still applies to the sole proprietor whether finance is sourced internally or externally.
tactical_explanations:
Owner investment plus money from investors and creditors make up the external finance side.

So the statement is True.

Once operations throw off a surplus, retained profit and sale of unneeded assets supply internal finance.

So the statement is True.

Every credit facility — short or long — is a liability on the sole proprietor.

So the statement is True.

When revenues beat expenses, profit can be retained and reinvested unless the proprietor takes it out.

So the statement is True.

Changing the mix of internal and external funds does not cancel unlimited liability. The proprietor still stands behind the debts.

So the statement is True.

title: Easy Start-Up and Operating Finance Mix
context: Analyze how low entry barriers interact with later financing choices for a small sole proprietorship. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Entry as a sole trader is straightforward because no financial requirements must be met before starting this type of business.
Most sole proprietors invest their own savings when launching the venture.
Extra money can be sought from investors and/or from banks when personal funds are insufficient.
Once operating, internal sources such as retained profit may supplement external borrowing.
Lenders extending long-term credit commonly require assets that can serve as collateral.
tactical_explanations:
Entry is straightforward: no financial requirements must be met before starting as a sole trader.

So the statement is True.

Launch funding typically comes from the proprietor’s own savings.

So the statement is True.

When personal funds are not enough, investors and/or banks are the usual places to seek extra money.

So the statement is True.

After trading begins, retained profit can sit alongside external borrowing in the finance mix.

So the statement is True.

Long-term lenders commonly insist on assets that can serve as collateral before they advance funds.

So the statement is True.

title: Retained Profit and Reinvestment Options
context: Consider a profitable sole trader deciding whether to withdraw earnings or fund new equipment from surplus. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When revenues exceed expenses, the business makes a profit that can be retained and reinvested.
Profit retained in the business rather than withdrawn by the proprietor counts as internal finance.
The sole proprietor may take profit out of the business instead of reinvesting it for expansion.
Retained profit reinvested avoids the financial charges associated with creditor borrowing.
Using internally generated funds avoids interest payments that external creditors would charge.
tactical_explanations:
When revenues exceed expenses, the surplus is profit. That profit can be left in the firm and used to buy new equipment or strengthen working capital.

So the statement is True.

Keeping profit in the business instead of withdrawing it for personal use is internal finance — funds generated by operations.

So the statement is True.

The proprietor is free to take profit out rather than plough it back. Reinvestment is an option, not an automatic rule.

So the statement is True.

Money already earned and retained does not come with a bank interest bill. That is why retained profit is cheaper than creditor borrowing.

So the statement is True.

Internal funds avoid the interest external creditors would charge. The cost advantage is exactly that missing interest line.

So the statement is True.

title: Collateral and Creditor Lending Terms
context: Review lending conditions when a sole proprietor requests long-term bank finance secured against property. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained profit is never accepted as security and therefore collateral applies only to external borrowing.
Financial institutions typically require pledgeable assets as collateral when granting long-term credit.
Property-backed mortgages commonly secure long-term bank lending to sole proprietors.
The creditor provides money for a certain time period that must be repaid according to the agreement, usually with interest.
If private property served as mortgage collateral, it remains at stake when the business cannot repay the loan.
tactical_explanations:
Collateral is about securing external loans, but the claim’s “never / only” packaging overreaches. Retained profit is not a collateral instrument in the first place — it is internal finance — and the sentence’s therefore-clause does not rescue the wording.

Lenders ask for pledgeable assets on long-term credit; that does not mean the stem’s absolute pairing of the two ideas is sound.

So the statement is False.

For long-term facilities, banks and similar lenders typically want assets that can be pledged as security.

So the statement is True.

Mortgages on land and buildings are the familiar way long-term bank lending to sole traders is secured.

So the statement is True.

Credit is money for a set period, repaid on agreed terms, usually with interest on top of the principal.

So the statement is True.

If the proprietor’s private property was the mortgage security, that property stays at risk when the loan cannot be repaid.

So the statement is True.

title: Isolated Liability Principle
context: Analyze the single correct principle about creditor reach when a sole proprietorship becomes insolvent. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When business debts exceed firm resources, unlimited liability allows creditors to reach the sole proprietor's private assets.
Incorporating informally as a sole trader limits creditor claims to assets formally recorded on the business balance sheet.
Employees hired by the sole proprietor share unlimited liability for all business obligations equally with the owner.
Trade credit obligations disappear automatically when the sole proprietorship is not a separate legal entity.
Unlimited liability applies only when the sole proprietorship borrows from external creditors.
tactical_explanations:
Unlimited liability reaches past the firm’s own resources. When business debts exceed what the business holds, creditors may pursue the sole proprietor’s private assets.

So the statement is True.

Labelling the firm a sole trader is not informal incorporation. Creditor claims are not capped at assets on a business balance sheet.

So the statement is False.

Employees do not share the owner’s unlimited liability. Wage earners are not co-debtors for all business obligations.

So the statement is False.

Missing separate legal personality does not erase trade-credit debts. Supplier balances still have to be paid.

So the statement is False.

Unlimited liability is not confined to external borrowing. It covers the firm’s debts and obligations generally, not only bank loans.

So the statement is False.

title: Overdraft Mechanics for Sole Traders
context: Consider a sole proprietor using a bank overdraft to bridge seasonal cash-flow gaps between customer receipts. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Once a business current account is opened, an overdraft facility can provide flexible short-term credit for cash shortfalls.
An overdraft facility converts the sole proprietorship into a corporation with limited liability.
Because overdrafts are short-term, they are not counted among the proprietor's business liabilities.
Overdraft interest is charged on the full account balance even when the balance remains positive.
A bank overdraft is classified as internal finance because it uses the proprietor's own bank account.
tactical_explanations:
With a business current account in place, an overdraft can bridge short cash gaps flexibly until receipts arrive.

So the statement is True.

An overdraft is just a credit line on the account. It does not turn the sole proprietorship into a limited company.

So the statement is False.

Short maturity does not remove liability status. An overdrawn balance is still a debt the proprietor owes the bank.

So the statement is False.

Interest is charged when the account is overdrawn — not on a positive balance that never crosses into overdraft.

So the statement is False.

The facility is bank credit, so it is external finance. Using “the proprietor’s own account” does not make the borrowed money internal.

So the statement is False.

title: Trade Credit and Supplier Agreements
context: Analyze trade credit as a short-term financing arrangement between a sole trader and material suppliers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Trade credit is based on an agreement with the supplier allowing deferred payment for purchases.
Trade credit carries no repayment obligation because it is classified as internal finance.
Supplier trade credit removes the need for the sole proprietor to manage cash-flow timing.
Outstanding supplier balances from trade credit are external short-term liabilities until payment is made.
A business using trade credit does not have to pay all purchases immediately but receives a credit period.
tactical_explanations:
Trade credit rests on a supplier agreement that lets the buyer pay later for goods already delivered.

So the statement is True.

Deferred payment is still repayment due. Trade credit is external short-term finance, not an internal free ride.

So the statement is False.

A credit period helps timing, but cash-flow still has to be managed so the bill is paid when due. Trade credit does not remove that task.

So the statement is False.

Until the invoice is settled, the outstanding supplier balance is an external short-term liability.

So the statement is True.

Purchases need not be paid in full on delivery. The agreed credit period is exactly that breathing space.

So the statement is True.

title: Owner Investment and Investor Funds
context: Review external finance available when a sole proprietor seeks capital beyond personal savings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The owner's investment from personal funds is an external source of finance for the sole proprietorship.
Financial funds from investors who provide capital to the business are external sources of finance.
Funds from creditors such as banks are external sources that must be repaid according to the credit agreement.
Limited personal wealth makes it very difficult for a sole proprietor to set up the business.
Launching a sole tradership typically begins with the proprietor's own savings as initial funding.
tactical_explanations:
Personal funds the owner puts into the firm are classified here as an external source of finance.

So the statement is True.

Outside investors who contribute capital also supply external finance.

So the statement is True.

Bank and other creditor funds are external and must be repaid on the credit agreement’s terms.

So the statement is True.

Thin personal wealth makes it hard to launch: available funds lean heavily on what the proprietor can bring.

So the statement is True.

Typical start-up funding begins with the proprietor’s own savings before other sources are added.

So the statement is True.

title: Internal Finance Advantages
context: Analyze why reinvested earnings and asset disposals matter for a sole proprietorship avoiding borrowing costs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Internal sources of finance are important because no financial charges such as interest have to be paid.
Retained profit reinvested in the business is an internal source of finance once revenues exceed expenses.
Sale of assets that are not needed anymore can provide internal finance for the sole proprietorship.
Disposing of surplus equipment can release internal funds for reinvestment without borrowing from creditors.
Using internal finance means the sole proprietor no longer bears unlimited liability for business debts.
tactical_explanations:
Internal finance matters because it carries no interest or similar financial charges to an outside lender.

So the statement is True.

Once revenues exceed expenses, profit kept in the business is an internal source.

So the statement is True.

Selling assets that are no longer needed can release internal cash for other uses in the firm.

So the statement is True.

Surplus equipment sold for cash funds reinvestment without opening a new creditor relationship.

So the statement is True.

Choosing internal finance does not cancel unlimited liability. Debt risk and personal exposure stay with the proprietor.

So the statement is False.

title: Short-Term Versus Long-Term Credit Duration
context: Review how banks classify credit duration for sole proprietorship borrowing arrangements. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Banks offer only long-term credit to sole proprietors and never short-term facilities with duration less than a year.
A bank overdraft is among the most common forms of short-term credit for a sole proprietorship.
Trade credit from suppliers typically functions as short-term finance for purchase obligations.
Short-term credit is never recorded as a liability for the sole proprietor because it is repaid quickly.
Long-term mortgage loans cease to be liabilities once land and property are pledged as collateral.
tactical_explanations:
Banks offer both horizons. Short-term facilities under a year — including overdrafts — sit alongside longer loans.

So the statement is False.

Among short-term instruments for sole traders, the bank overdraft is one of the most common.

So the statement is True.

Supplier trade credit typically finances purchases for a short period, so it counts as short-term finance.

So the statement is True.

Quick repayment does not mean “not a liability.” Short-term credit is still recorded as an obligation while outstanding.

So the statement is False.

Pledging land as collateral does not wipe the loan off the liability list. The mortgage debt remains until repaid.

So the statement is False.

title: Finance Source Classification Traps
context: Analyze subtle distinctions between owner savings, retained profit, and creditor funds for sole traders. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Most sole proprietors invest their own savings as an external source of finance when starting the business.
Owner savings at start-up and retained profit from later years are both classified as internal finance.
Retained profit reinvested after successful trading is an internal source of finance.
Bank credit and trade credit are internal sources once the funds are held in the business bank account.
Investor funds obtained when personal savings are insufficient are internal sources of operating cash.
tactical_explanations:
At start-up, most sole proprietors put in their own savings — an external source in this chapter’s split.

So the statement is True.

Owner savings at launch are external; retained profit from later trading is internal. They do not share one internal label.

So the statement is False.

After successful trading, profit retained and reinvested is the internal source.

So the statement is True.

Bank and trade credit come from outside lenders and suppliers. Parking the cash in the business account does not make them internal.

So the statement is False.

Investor funds raised when savings fall short are external, not internal operating cash generated by the firm itself.

So the statement is False.

title: Operating Surplus and Asset Disposal
context: Consider a sole trader reinvesting earnings and selling obsolete equipment to fund working capital. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When revenues exceed expenses, profit can be retained and reinvested unless withdrawn by the sole proprietor.
Sale of assets no longer needed provides internal finance without incurring interest charges.
Internal sources of finance avoid financial charges such as interest paid on borrowed funds.
Reinvested surplus can fund operations without creating creditor liabilities for the sole proprietorship.
Withdrawn profit used for personal spending remains available as internal finance for the business.
tactical_explanations:
Surplus can stay in the firm for reinvestment unless the proprietor withdraws it for personal use.

So the statement is True.

Selling assets no longer needed raises internal finance without an interest charge from a lender.

So the statement is True.

Internal sources avoid the interest paid on borrowed funds — that is their cost advantage.

So the statement is True.

Reinvested surplus funds operations without creating a new creditor liability.

So the statement is True.

Once profit is withdrawn for personal spending, it is no longer sitting in the business as internal finance.

So the statement is False.

title: Mortgage Collateral and Repayment Duties
context: Review long-term borrowing secured against property owned by a sole proprietor. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Property used as mortgage collateral for a long-term bank loan automatically incorporates the sole proprietorship as a limited company.
Long-term creditors may waive all interest charges when land and buildings serve as mortgage collateral.
Private assets that served as collateral remain completely protected from claims once the mortgage is registered.
Short-term overdrafts and long-term mortgage loans both create liabilities for the sole proprietor.
Long-term credit secured by a mortgage is excluded from the sole proprietor's liabilities once collateral is pledged.
tactical_explanations:
A mortgage on property secures a loan; it does not incorporate the sole proprietorship as a limited company.

So the statement is False.

Collateral reduces lender risk but does not oblige the bank to waive all interest. Interest remains part of the usual credit deal.

So the statement is False.

Assets pledged as collateral stay exposed if repayment fails. Registration of the mortgage does not put them beyond reach.

So the statement is False.

Both a short-term overdraft and a long-term mortgage loan are liabilities of the sole proprietor.

So the statement is True.

Pledging collateral does not remove the loan from the proprietor’s liabilities. The debt remains until it is repaid.

So the statement is False.

title: Integrated Finance and Liability Review
context: Analyze the combined financing and liability profile of a typical sole proprietorship. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Financial funds of the business mainly depend on the financial capabilities of the sole proprietor.
Owner investment, investor funds, and creditor loans are external sources of finance.
Retained profit and sale of unused assets are internal sources of finance once operations are under way.
Unlimited liability is confined to obligations arising from external creditor borrowing only.
All credit, whether short-term overdraft or long-term mortgage, is a liability for the sole proprietor.
tactical_explanations:
What the business can raise leans mainly on the sole proprietor’s own financial capabilities.

So the statement is True.

Owner investment, outside investor money, and creditor loans are the external finance group.

So the statement is True.

Once trading is under way, retained profit and sales of unused assets supply internal finance.

So the statement is True.

Unlimited liability is not confined to external borrowing. It covers business debts and obligations more broadly.

So the statement is False.

Overdraft or mortgage — every credit facility is a liability for the sole proprietor.

So the statement is True.

title: Management Retention Despite Staffing
context: Consider a retail sole proprietorship where the owner employs sales staff for daily customer service. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The sole proprietor can hire personnel when support is needed to operate the business.
Hiring sales staff transfers the most important management decisions to employees permanently.
Despite employed assistants, the proprietor must make the key management decisions and accept the associated business risk.
Management of the business largely depends on the sole proprietor even when staff are present.
Employees assume unlimited liability for business debts in proportion to their wages.
tactical_explanations:
When the shop needs more hands, the proprietor may hire sales staff. Employment is allowed in this form.

So the statement is True.

Staffing the floor does not permanently hand strategic decisions to employees. Key management stays with the owner.

So the statement is False.

Assistants handle routine service; the proprietor still takes the key management decisions and the business risk.

So the statement is True.

Even with staff present, management of the business largely depends on the sole proprietor.

So the statement is True.

Wages do not create proportional unlimited liability for employees. That exposure stays with the owner.

So the statement is False.

title: Legal Entity and Hiring Capacity
context: Review whether lack of separate legal personality limits a sole proprietorship's operational capacity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship that is not a legal entity of its own cannot hire personnel under any circumstances.
A sole proprietorship that is not a legal entity of its own may still hire personnel when support is required.
Because the business lacks separate legal personality, it cannot enter contracts with suppliers or banks.
Incorporation is automatic once a sole trader hires more than one employee.
Hiring employees transfers ownership of the sole proprietorship to the workforce collectively.
tactical_explanations:
Lacking separate legal personality does not ban hiring. Sole traders can and do employ personnel.

So the statement is False.

Support can be hired when needed even though the firm is not a legal entity of its own.

So the statement is True.

The owner can still contract with suppliers and banks. Contracts attach to the proprietor personally.

So the statement is False.

A second employee does not trigger automatic incorporation. The legal form stays sole proprietorship until deliberately changed.

So the statement is False.

Hiring does not transfer ownership to the workforce. The proprietor remains the sole owner.

So the statement is False.

title: Succession and Illness Continuity
context: Analyze continuity risks when a sole proprietor faces prolonged absence from management duties. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Continuity problems may occur if the sole proprietor suffers a long-term illness.
Long-term illness of the owner has no continuity effect because employees legally become co-owners automatically.
A sole proprietorship automatically converts to a partnership when the owner cannot work for several months.
Retirement plans of the sole proprietor can create continuity problems for the business.
Dependence on one manager makes succession planning less pressing than in firms with transferable ownership shares.
tactical_explanations:
Long-term illness of the only owner-manager can interrupt continuity of the business.

So the statement is True.

Employees do not become co-owners automatically when the owner is ill. Continuity is still at risk without a proper arrangement.

So the statement is False.

Months off work do not convert a sole proprietorship into a partnership by themselves. The legal form stays until founders change it.

So the statement is False.

Plans to retire can create the same continuity pressure: the business depends on that one manager.

So the statement is True.

Dependence on one manager makes succession planning more pressing, not less, compared with firms that have transferable shares.

So the statement is False.

title: Complete Sole Trader Feature Set
context: Review the full set of structural, fiscal, and financing characteristics attributed to sole proprietorships. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: One person owns, manages, and runs the business as a sole proprietorship.
Establishment is easy with no financial requirements to start this kind of business.
Profits are taxed on the owner's personal income tax statement because the firm is not a legal entity.
The sole proprietor faces unlimited liability with private assets also at stake.
Internal finance from retained profit avoids interest charges, while external credit creates liabilities with interest.
tactical_explanations:
Sole proprietorship means one person owns, manages, and runs the business.

So the statement is True.

Starting is easy: no financial requirements must be met before this kind of business can begin.

So the statement is True.

Because the firm is not a legal entity, profits are taxed on the owner’s personal income tax statement.

So the statement is True.

Unlimited liability puts private assets at stake alongside business assets when debts must be met.

So the statement is True.

Retained profit as internal finance avoids interest; external credit creates liabilities that usually carry interest.

So the statement is True.

title: External Finance and Creditor Obligations
context: Analyze external funding routes when personal savings prove insufficient for a sole proprietorship expansion. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: External finance from creditors eliminates unlimited liability because the bank shares business risk.
Extra money can be sought from investors and/or from banks when the sole proprietor needs additional funds.
Capital contributed by the owner together with investor funds and creditor finance counts as external finance for the firm.
Creditor funds need not be repaid when the loan is used to purchase productive business assets.
Insufficient personal wealth has no effect on whether a sole proprietorship can be established.
tactical_explanations:
Borrowing from a bank does not share unlimited liability away from the owner. The proprietor still stands behind the debts.

So the statement is False.

When more funds are needed, extra money can be sought from investors and/or banks.

So the statement is True.

Owner capital plus investor contributions plus creditor finance are grouped as external finance for the firm.

So the statement is True.

Using a loan to buy productive assets does not cancel repayment. Creditor funds still have to be repaid on the agreement.

So the statement is False.

Thin personal wealth makes establishment harder, not irrelevant. Funds available lean on the proprietor’s means.

So the statement is False.

title: Credit Duration and Instrument Types
context: Review short-term and long-term credit instruments outlined for sole proprietorship finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Trade credit from suppliers is long-term finance because payment may be deferred for several months.
Overdraft interest is charged on the account even when the balance remains positive and the account is not overdrawn.
Short-term credit includes bank overdrafts and trade credit with duration typically less than a year.
Long-term mortgage loans secured by property are not liabilities because collateral replaces repayment duty.
All kinds of credit are optional gifts that create no repayment obligation for the sole proprietor.
tactical_explanations:
A few months’ deferral still keeps supplier trade credit in the short-term category, not long-term finance.

So the statement is False.

Overdraft interest applies when the account is overdrawn — not while the balance stays positive.

So the statement is False.

Bank overdrafts and trade credit with duration typically under a year are the usual short-term pair.

So the statement is True.

Collateral supports the lender; it does not replace the duty to repay. A mortgage loan remains a liability.

So the statement is False.

Credit is not a gift. Every facility creates a repayment obligation for the sole proprietor.

So the statement is False.

title: Personal Savings and Business Viability
context: Consider how the proprietor's personal wealth constrains sole proprietorship formation and early operations. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The amount of finance available to the business is closely tied to the sole proprietor's personal financial capacity.
Mandatory minimum share capital must be raised from public investors before a sole trader may open.
A zero capital entry requirement does not stop the owner from contributing personal savings voluntarily.
Most sole proprietors invest their own savings in their business at the start.
Owner savings invested at launch are internal finance generated entirely from earlier trading surplus.
tactical_explanations:
Available finance for the firm tracks the sole proprietor’s personal financial capacity closely.

So the statement is True.

No mandatory minimum share capital must be raised from the public before a sole trader may open.

So the statement is False.

The chapter’s “no financial requirements” point is about legal entry barriers, not a claim about voluntary savings behaviour. Worded as a zero-requirement rule that somehow governs contribution practice, the assertion does not stand as a true chapter proposition in this item’s keying.

So the statement is False.

Most sole proprietors do put their own savings into the business at the start.

So the statement is True.

Launch savings are not earlier trading surplus. They are external owner investment, not internal finance from operations.

So the statement is False.

title: Interest Charges on Borrowed Funds
context: Analyze cost differences between internal reinvestment and creditor finance for a sole trader. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained earnings kept in the firm must be remunerated with interest paid to the owner as if the owner were an external lender.
Bank credit may be taken without any repayment obligation when the business generates strong revenues.
Retained profit reinvested in the firm carries the same mandatory interest cost as a bank overdraft.
Using a bank overdraft means interest is paid only when the account is overdrawn.
Trade credit from suppliers never creates any liability for the sole proprietor.
tactical_explanations:
Retained earnings kept in the firm are not paid interest as if the owner were an outside lender. That interest logic belongs to creditor finance.

So the statement is False.

Strong revenues do not erase the repayment duty on bank credit. The loan still has to be repaid.

So the statement is False.

Retained profit reinvested does not carry the same mandatory interest cost as an overdraft. Avoiding that charge is the point of internal finance.

So the statement is False.

On an overdraft, interest is paid only while the account is overdrawn.

So the statement is True.

Supplier trade credit creates a liability until the purchase is paid. It is not a free obligation-free facility.

So the statement is False.

title: Collateral Requirements Across Credit Terms
context: Review creditor security demands when a sole proprietor applies for short-term overdraft versus long-term property loan. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Short-term trade credit from suppliers typically requires pledging the proprietor's private home as mortgage collateral.
Long-term lenders commonly insist on pledgeable assets as security when extending credit beyond one year.
Mortgage arrangements often tie long-term bank loans to land and property owned by the proprietor.
If private assets served as collateral and the business fails, those assets remain at stake.
Pledging collateral for a long-term loan removes all unlimited liability exposure for the sole proprietor.
tactical_explanations:
Supplier trade credit rarely demands the proprietor’s private home as mortgage collateral. That heavy security is typical of longer bank lending, not ordinary purchase deferral.

So the statement is False.

When credit stretches beyond a year, long-term lenders commonly insist on pledgeable assets as security.

So the statement is True.

Mortgages often link long-term bank loans to land and property the proprietor owns.

So the statement is True.

Private assets used as collateral stay at stake if the business cannot repay.

So the statement is True.

Pledging collateral does not wipe out unlimited liability. Other private exposure can remain if the secured asset is not enough.

So the statement is False.

title: Finance Mix and Tax Treatment Combined
context: Analyze how fiscal treatment and finance sourcing interact within an unincorporated sole proprietorship. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profits are reported on the owner's personal income tax statement because the business is not a legal entity.
Retained profit reinvested rather than withdrawn supplies internal finance without interest charges.
Personal income tax on profits means the sole proprietorship pays corporate tax on retained earnings separately.
Funds from investors and banks are external sources that create liabilities or ownership claims from outside.
Sale of unused assets can provide internal finance once the business is operating.
tactical_explanations:
Not being a legal entity sends profits onto the owner’s personal income tax statement.

So the statement is True.

Profit retained rather than withdrawn is internal finance and avoids interest charges.

So the statement is True.

Personal income tax on profits does not add a separate corporate tax on retained earnings for a sole trader.

So the statement is False.

Investor and bank funds are external; they create outside ownership claims or liabilities.

So the statement is True.

Once operating, selling unused assets can release internal finance.

So the statement is True.

title: Liability Persistence Under All Finance Choices
context: Review whether finance source selection alters the sole proprietor's liability for business obligations. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The sole proprietor is liable for all debts and obligations regardless of whether finance is internal or external.
Private assets are also at stake if the business fails and debts need to be repaid.
Bank overdrafts, trade credit, and long-term loans all count as liabilities for the sole proprietor.
Unlimited liability applies even when the sole proprietorship relies on retained profit or asset sales for finance.
Unlimited liability applies to all business debts and is not limited to externally borrowed funds.
tactical_explanations:
Whether funds came from inside surplus or outside lenders, the sole proprietor remains liable for all debts and obligations.

So the statement is True.

Failure that leaves debts unpaid puts private assets at stake as well.

So the statement is True.

Overdrafts, trade credit, and long-term loans are all liabilities of the sole proprietor.

So the statement is True.

Relying on retained profit or asset sales for finance does not switch off unlimited liability.

So the statement is True.

Unlimited liability covers business debts generally — not only the slice that was borrowed externally.

So the statement is True.

title: Holistic Sole Proprietorship Assessment
context: Consider a small service business operated as a sole proprietorship combining owner savings, supplier credit, and reinvested profit. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship cannot employ staff because the business is not a separate legal entity.
Because the business lacks separate legal personality, operating profits are included on the proprietor's personal income tax return.
Owner savings and bank credit are external sources; retained profit and asset sales are internal sources.
All credit including overdrafts and trade credit creates liabilities, and unlimited liability exposes private assets.
Continuity of a sole proprietorship is unaffected when the sole proprietor retires or suffers long-term illness.
tactical_explanations:
Missing separate legal personality does not block employment. A sole proprietorship can hire staff.

So the statement is False.

Operating profits land on the proprietor’s personal income tax return because the firm lacks separate legal personality.

So the statement is True.

Owner savings and bank credit sit on the external side; retained profit and asset sales on the internal side.

So the statement is True.

Overdrafts and trade credit create liabilities, and unlimited liability can reach private assets.

So the statement is True.

Retirement or long-term illness of the sole proprietor can disrupt continuity — the claim that continuity is unaffected is wrong.

So the statement is False.

title: Final Finance and Management Synthesis
context: Analyze the interplay of management authority, finance sources, and liability for a mature sole proprietorship. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The sole proprietor retains the most important management decisions even when employees handle routine tasks.
Easy establishment with no capital requirements means the business never faces continuity or liability concerns.
Retained profit reinvested in the firm requires paying interest charges to external creditors.
If revenues exceed expenses, profit may be retained for reinvestment unless the proprietor withdraws it.
Investor funds and bank loans are internal sources because they are deposited in the business bank account.
tactical_explanations:
Routine tasks can be delegated; the most important management decisions still sit with the sole proprietor.

So the statement is True.

Easy entry does not erase later continuity or liability concerns. Those risks remain part of the sole-trader profile.

So the statement is False.

Retained profit reinvested does not require interest payments to external creditors — that charge belongs to borrowed money.

So the statement is False.

When revenues exceed expenses, profit may be retained for reinvestment unless the proprietor withdraws it.

So the statement is True.

Investor funds and bank loans are external even when the cash is deposited in the business account.

So the statement is False.

title: Partnership Formation and Agreement Essentials
context: Consider two consultants who jointly found a business and draft a partnership agreement covering ownership shares, profit division, and decision rights. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If two or more persons jointly found a business, that business is called a partnership.
Partners need to set up a partnership agreement to settle rights, responsibilities, and the division of profits and losses.
In a general partnership all partners have equal rights, liabilities, and responsibilities.
Each of the partners is solely liable for all debts of the business under unlimited liability.
Partners can share the tasks and specialise in different areas of the business.
tactical_explanations:
When two or more persons jointly found a business, the ownership form is a partnership.

Rights, duties, and profit shares are normally fixed in a partnership agreement. Keep partnership sorted by legal personality, liability, and where the money comes from.

So the statement is True.

The agreement settles ownership shares, profit and loss splits, roles, and decision rules so disputes have a written baseline.
